about.title: Personal Injury Help in Westmorland, California

Reported collisions here have tended to cluster on Monday nights into early Monday morning, between roughly 12 a.m. and 2 a.m. If you or someone in your family was hurt in a crash, a fall, or another accident in or near Westmorland, we can help you take the next step. We handle personal injury cases on a contingency-fee basis, meaning there's no upfront cost — fees only apply if we recover money on your behalf. Our team reviews your situation, advises you on your options, and represents your interests throughout the process. There's no cost and no pressure to reach out and find out where you stand.

whyChoose.title: Why People in Westmorland Choose Us

items.title: You Have a Limited Window to Act
items.desc: California generally gives injured people two years from the date of an accident to file a claim, though claims against a government entity can require action in as little as six months. Reaching out sooner helps preserve your options.

items.title: Shared Fault Doesn't End Your Claim
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still pursue compensation even if you were partly responsible for an accident — your recovery is simply reduced by your share of fault, not eliminated.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: In most ordinary injury cases, California places no limit on non-economic damages such as pain and suffering, meaning your claim's value isn't artificially capped by state law.

items.title: No Fee Unless You Recover
items.desc: We work on contingency, so you don't pay out of pocket to have your case reviewed or handled — fees only come from money recovered on your behalf.

items.question: How long do I have to file an injury claim in Westmorland?
items.answer: In most California injury cases, you have two years from the date of the accident to file a lawsuit. If your claim involves a government entity, such as a city or county road issue, that window can shrink to as little as six months, so it's wise not to wait.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California follows a pure comparative fault rule, which means you can still recover compensation even if you share some blame. Your total recovery is simply reduced by your percentage of fault, rather than blocked entirely.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to happen in Westmorland?
items.answer: Public collision records point to Rt 85, 6th Street, 8th Street, and W Main Street as the corridors with the most recorded crash activity, with reports skewing toward Monday nights between about midnight and 2 a.m. These are simply the counts on record, not a judgment about any road's safety.

items.question: Will I owe money upfront to speak with an attorney?
items.answer: No. Our consultation is free, and we work on contingency. That means fees only apply if we recover compensation for you.

items.answer: Contact us for a free case review. We'll evaluate your situation, explain your options, and advise you on next steps — all at no cost and with no obligation.
